uncertain.text: de tous les parens. dequoy rendra certain teſmoigna-
uncertain.note: the point after 'parens' is read as a period (round, on the baseline) although the sentence runs on into 'dequoy'; sic, no correction made.

uncertain.text: manifeſter Amphiaraus ſon mari {e}, qu's'eſtoit caché pour
uncertain.note: the body's fifth marker (alphabet b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i requires an 'e' between {d} at 'argent' and {f} at 'diſant') is not clearly resolved as a distinct glyph at this resolution; best reading places it directly after 'mari', where a small italic letter appears to merge visually with the following apostrophe+s of 'qu's'eſtoit'. The margin note assigned to key 'e' (Ciceron's sixth Verrine; Virgil Aeneid VI) matches this Amphiaraus/Eryphyle passage thematically, supporting the placement, but the marker's exact shape and the reading 'qu's'eſtoit' (vs. 'qu'il s'eſtoit') are both uncertain.

uncertain.text: n'aller poinr a la guerre de Thebes, de peur d'eſtre tué
uncertain.note: 'poinr' for 'point' (r for t, a wrong sort); transcribed as printed, sic.

uncertain.text: oncques de ſi grant vehemence, que l'auarice, mere,
uncertain.note: a faint small mark appears near 'auarice' before 'mere' that could be a stray letter or ink artifact rather than a true marker; no unused key letter remains between {g} (at 'vertu' above) and {h} (at 'maux' below) to assign it to, so it is transcribed as plain punctuation. Flagged in case it is in fact an unrecorded marker.
a small mark sits close beside the italic 'i' marker, possibly the marker's own dot rendered low/right, possibly a separate fleck; read as a single marker 'i' with no additional key.

printed with a wide justification gap as 'Mart in'; normalized to the single word 'Martin' (the name is unambiguous and appears elsewhere in the text unsplit), per the convention that compositor's spacing is not reproduced.

the heading is read as 'ANNOT. XV.' by analogy with 'ANNOTAT. XIII.'/'ANNOTAT. XIIII.' on the preceding pages, but the point after 'ANNOT' is not fully certain to be present at this resolution; it could print as 'ANNOT XV.' without it.
roman numeral read as 'xxvuij'; could be 'xxvij' (27) or 'xxviij' (28) — the v/u/i sequence is small and the glyphs run together.

chapter read as 'ix' (9); the Vulgate/Epistle passage on avarice as 'root of all evils' is 1 Timothy chapter 6, so 'ix' may be a misprint for 'vi' (sic) or may be a genuine paragraph/section reference rather than the chapter; transcribed as printed.
the point after the citation abbreviation 'l' (lex) prints as a comma-shaped mark rather than a round period; transcribed as printed, sic.
a faint tilde-like mark over the final vowel is read as the standard n/m-omission tilde (ſeruitutẽ = ſeruitutem); at this resolution it could also be a worn accent or printer's fleck.
